title: View Transitions Integration: hx-swap="transition:true" Animation Coordination

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When a page swaps content, it usually flickers or snaps abruptly. By adding `transition:true`, HTMX asks the browser to take a quick screenshot of the old content, swap the HTML smoothly in the background, and cross-fade or slide between the two screenshots like a native mobile app.
progressiveExplaining.junior: HTMX natively integrates with the browser's View Transitions API. By adding the `transition:true` modifier to `hx-swap` (e.g. `hx-swap="innerHTML transition:true"`), HTMX wraps the DOM mutation inside `document.startViewTransition()`. You can then customize the animation using standard CSS pseudo-elements like `::view-transition-old(root)` and `::view-transition-new(root)`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `transition:true` bridges server-rendered HTML partials with GPU-accelerated browser view transitions. When the HTTP response arrives, HTMX checks if `document.startViewTransition` is supported. If available, it captures the current layer snapshots, executes the swap inside the transition update callback, and lets the browser's compositor smoothly crossfade or morph elements sharing a `view-transition-name`.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In the swap engine, if `swapStyle.transition` is true and `document.startViewTransition` exists, HTMX calls `document.startViewTransition(() => { performActualDOMSwap(); })`. If the browser does not support the API, HTMX gracefully falls back to executing `performActualDOMSwap()` immediately, ensuring zero breakage on older browsers.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you enable View Transitions globally for all HTMX swaps without writing `transition:true` on every element?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of HTMX global configuration flags.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Set the global configuration flag in JavaScript: **`htmx.config.globalViewTransitions = true;`**. This automatically wraps every `hx-swap` operation across the entire application in `document.startViewTransition()` whenever supported by the client browser.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If using `globalViewTransitions = true`, ensure your CSS doesn't accidentally assign duplicate `view-transition-name` properties to multiple elements simultaneously, or the transition will fail.

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if an element with a `view-transition-name` exists in multiple places on the screen during a swap?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of browser View Transitions API constraints.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: The W3C View Transitions spec strictly requires that **`view-transition-name` values must be unique on the page at any given moment**. If two active elements share the same `view-transition-name` (e.g. `view-transition-name: card`), the browser aborts the view transition entirely and performs an instant non-animated DOM swap.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Never assign static `view-transition-name: item` to items in a list loop; dynamically assign unique names (e.g. `style="view-transition-name: item-101"`).
